recipes.name: Avocado-Mango Salsa
ingredients_raw: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced

steps.text: Toss mango, bell pepper, onion, vinegar, sugar, and olive oil together in a bowl; gently fold in avocado. Season with salt.

raw_recipe.headline: Avocado-Mango Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy avocado-mango salsa recipe features fresh bell peppers and red onion — it makes a tasty dip that comes together in only 30 minutes.
raw_recipe.name: Avocado-Mango Salsa
recipeIngredient: 1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced

recipeInstructions.text: Toss mango, bell pepper, onion, vinegar, sugar, and olive oil together in a bowl; gently fold in avocado. Season with salt.

review.reviewBody: Wow! I had a baby shower with way too many appetizers - the only one that was gone was this mango salsa. Costco has some delicious pre cut mango that made this super easy and delicious. Definitely let it sit in the refrigerator for about an hour before to get the full flavor.

Used 1/4 of a small onion, omitted salt, and used lime juice instead of vinegar. I also added a whole jalapeno for a little heat. This was great. I mixed everything together other than the avocado and let it sit in the fridge for 8 hours. Right before I was going to serve I added the avocado. This recipe was a hit at the party. TFS
I added about a tsp of lime juice. My girlfriend who gave me the recipe, processed it in her blender for a couple of pulses. I prefer it chunky!

I have never made salsa before and was looking for a tasty mango salsa to compliment a quick late evening cod fish dinner. As I'm trying to do less sugar these days, I knew I would eliminate that. I also used "Naples.." suggestion and use real lime juice instead of vinegar, added cilantro (one of my favorite herbs) and I also decided to reduced the salt to 1/2 tsp--it was spot on delicious and upon taste test made me do dance! Great recipe! My family loved it! I will try this w/ my salmon cakes and other dishes too.

Great as a reference or starting point, but as is the case with many recipes I adjusted the recipe to suit my own tastes. I eliminated the sugar - for me it was totally unnecessary and may have even been counterproductive. In keeping with the tropical flair of the recipe I substituted fresh lime juice for the vinegar (loved that!) and added some chopped fresh cilantro. For my tastes, four stars as written and an unequivocal five stars with my modifications. Served this alongside crab cakes and there couldn't have been a more ideal accompaniment.

This was a pretty good starting point, but I did make some changes. Omitted the sugar, replaced the vinegar with lime juice, I used sweet Vidalia onion and I added 1 small, lightly roasted jalapeno for a little heat. I made it well ahead of time so the flavors could meld and added the diced avocado right before serving. Thanks, Julie - this is a keeper.

To make more, I added another mango, 1 large fresh tomato and 1 can of diced tomatoes with chilis, and another can of diced tomatoes (Fennel and Red Pepper), 4 garlic cloves, cup of cilantro, a little more sugar, and another onion, the juice of 1 lime. I let it sit overnight and serve it over baked salmon, or even store bought rotisserie chicken with tortilla chips and rice! Yummo. 
Thanks for the recipe.

3 stars as written...after tasting it, I added a finely diced jalapeno, a couple of squeezes of fresh lime juice (instead of vinegar), and a handful of chopped FRESH cilantro and it became 5+ stars. It's even better after a few hours in the frig. You can actually omit the oil completely if you wish. This is a favorite in south Texas and so delicious as a dip, a fish/chicken/pork/steak topper or just by the spoonful!

I have been a long time lurker here on allrecipes but I had to write a review for this! I read a lot of reviews and followed their advice to put in half of the oil and half of the vinegar plus a second mango and avocado just because we love them both so much and it was FANTASTIC! Served with chicken, jasmine rice and steamed veggies. What a perfect meal.
I picked this over the other recipes. I used 2 mangos and 1T vinegar and 1 T lime, and reduced the salt. I am including this in our community newsletter. Yes, can't stop eating it.

Wow - beautiful, healthy, tasty! Modifications -- - Substitute juice of 1 lime for vinegar; - Start with 1/2 tsp salt and go up -- 1 tsp salt is too much for almost any recipe - Would probably be fine w/2 tsp olive oil - 1 Tbs was a little too much.

I switched a few things up with this recipe. Instead of regular sugar I used organic raw sugar. Instead of a red onion, I used a sweet white onion. Then, I cut 2 different color peppers up a full avocado and frozen mango chunks I defrosted. I mix it in a large bowl. My friends and family love it. We use it on everything, rice, steak, mahi mahi, boneless skinless chicken breasts, buggers too. We go avocado mango salsa crazy!
Very good. Gonna serve over pork carnitas!!!
This was beautiful, and the flavor was delicious... mangos are not easy to work with!
Very good! I added shrimp at the end and served it on Boston lettuce, refreshing and low cal! Thanks!
delicious! used more mango and added jalapeños
I used apple cider vinegar-because thats all i had---OMG it went perfect with Jamaican jerk chicken, my husband was amazed. PLEASE TRY IT--ESPECIALLY WITH JERK CHICKEN!!!
Absolutely loved it. I did add cilantro to it. Will be making this regularly.
Used only 1 scallion and 2 small peppers (about 1/2 pepper called for). Was wonderful.
wow so easy to make, everyone really enjoyed it
